The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the narrative's emotional core. In the first third of the story, the author uses **compression of time** to summarize roughly twenty years—spanning college, early careers, marriages, and divorces—in just six paragraphs. This brisk pacing effectively establishes the mythology of "Q" as an untouchable, effortlessly successful figure over a long period. 

Then, the narrative shifts dramatically, slowing down to focus on a single morning at a hotel pool. By dedicating the majority of the story's length to this one-hour interaction (and its immediate aftermath), the author uses a relative **stretching of time** to emphasize the weight of the moment. The slow, detailed examination of Q's awkwardness—the failed Marcus Aurelius quote, the disintegrating napkin, the slump of his shoulders—contrasts sharply with the breezy summary of his previous decades of perfection. This shift in pacing allows the reader to feel the profound shift in the narrator's twenty-year perception of his friend, making the climax earned and resonant.
